Pigsy bakes nine little cookies on
a tray. He counts them: one, two,
three, four, five, six, seven, eight,
nine! The cookies all look
the same.
2

Wukong and Rabbit come to visit
Pigsy. Pigsy puts out three plates,
one for each friend. “Let’s share
the cookies!” he says.
3

“I can do it!” says Wukong. He
puts four cookies on his own plate,
three on Rabbit’s and only two
on Pigsy’s.
4

Pigsy looks at his plate for a long
time. “My plate has so much
empty room,” he says. “My two
cookies look lonely!”
5

Rabbit counts the cookies on each
plate: four, three and two. “That
is not fair,” she says. “Each friend
should get the same number.”
6

So everyone puts the cookies back
on the tray. They count again,
and there are still nine. Not one
cookie is lost.
7

“Let’s share in turns,” says
Rabbit. “One cookie goes on each
plate, and then we go
round again.”
8

In round one, Rabbit puts one
cookie on each plate. Wukong,
Rabbit and Pigsy each get one.
Six cookies are still on the tray.
9

In round two, each plate gets one
more. Now every plate has two,
and three are left.
10

In round three, the last three
cookies go on the plates. Now the
tray is empty!
11

Everyone counts the cookies on
their own plate. Wukong has
three, Rabbit has three, and Pigsy
has three. “We all have the same,
so it is fair!” says Rabbit.
12

Pigsy turns the empty tray over
and looks under it. “I am looking
for a fourth plate,” he says very
seriously. “It is for my tummy!”
13

Rabbit giggles. “There is no
fourth plate, Pigsy. Three plates
are just right for three friends.”
14

Now it is time to eat, and
everyone takes a big bite. Crunch!
Each friend has an equal share.
15

Soon there are only crumbs on
the three plates. Pigsy pats his
round tummy and smiles. “Three
cookies each was just right,”
he says.
16
